title: Signed inner product as agreements minus Hamming distance
statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be two $n$-bit strings. Their signed inner product $\langle x, y\rangle$ is the integer $\sum_{i} \varepsilon_i$, where $\varepsilon_i = +1$ at each coordinate $i$ on which $x_i = y_i$ and $\varepsilon_i = -1$ at each coordinate on which $x_i \neq y_i$. Writing $a(x,y)$ for the agreement count of $x$ and $y$, the number of coordinates on which they agree, and $d_H(x,y)$ for the Hamming distance between them, the number of coordinates on which they differ, one has
\[
  \langle x, y\rangle \;=\; a(x,y) - d_H(x,y),
\]
an equality of integers in which the two counts are regarded as integers.
hypotheses_covered: x and y are n-bit strings
replaced:
For any two $n$-bit strings $x$ and $y$,
\[
  \mathrm{signedInner}(x, y) \;=\; \mathrm{agreementCount}(x, y) - \mathrm{hammingDist}(x, y).
\]
That is, the signed inner product equals the number of agreeing coordinates minus
the number of disagreeing coordinates.
